Description: Surrogate key; the id every invoice references.
Why: US-01-002 AC1: an invoice names its customer, and a random id leaves nothing to guess in a URL.

Description: The tenant that owns this customer; every query filters on it.
Why: Rule: tenant isolation. A customer is visible only inside its tenant (US-01-001 AC3).
US-01-001 AC1: the add-customer form requires a name; US-01-002 AC2 prints it on the invoice.

Description: Address the invoice is sent to.
Why: US-01-002 AC4: sending an invoice emails the customer; US-01-001 AC2: a duplicate email in one tenant is refused.
Rule: every table carries timestamptz audit columns (database postgres reference).
Rule: every table carries timestamptz audit columns (database postgres reference).

Description: Surrogate key; the id in the invoice URL.
Why: US-01-003 AC1: the invoice page is addressed by id.

Description: The tenant that issued the invoice; leads every list index.
Why: Rule: tenant isolation, and tenant_id first in composite keys (US-01-003 AC2).
US-01-002 AC1: every invoice has exactly one customer. RESTRICT so a customer with invoices cannot vanish.

Description: Lifecycle: draft, sent, paid or void.
Why: US-01-003 AC3: the list filters by status; US-01-002 AC4: sending moves draft to sent.

Description: Total in minor units of currency (cents, paise).
Why: US-01-002 AC2: the invoice shows a total; rule: money is an integer in minor units.
US-01-002 AC2: the total is shown with its currency; an amount without one is ambiguous.

Description: Calendar date payment is due, in the tenant's time zone.
Why: US-01-003 AC4: overdue invoices are flagged after the due date.
US-01-003 AC2: the list is ordered newest first.
Rule: every table carries timestamptz audit columns (database postgres reference).
